texts.facts: In this case, a detailed accident report was filed by police in terms of provisions of Motor Vehicle Act and same is treated as Claim Petition in view of the provisions contained in such Act. 2. As per the investigation by the police officials, a PCR call was received and police officials reached at the spot but no accident was found to take place. In the meanwhile, intimation from Appollo hospital, Delhi was received regarding injured Master Umang who was aged 3 years 6 months and it was further informed that patient had gone to AIIMS Trauma Center. Later on, his father namely Shiv Kumar gave her statement that he is running a Tea shop at about 7.30 pm on 20.08.2017. He was at his shop and his minor child/victim Umang was playing on service road. At that time, one Master Umang Kumar (Minor) vs Rajdeep Mishra on 25 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100853402/ 1 motorcyclist bearing no. DL-3SBS-9175 came in a rash and negligent manner and before such father could take away such child from that place, such motorcyclist hit the child. The complainant/father further stated that such motorcyclist stopped after a while but thereafter run away and in the meanwhile, police brought the injured child to Apollo hospital. Later on, identity of such driver was determined during investigation. 3. The police after investigation in present case filed charge sheet for offence u/s 279,338 IPC against the respondent/driver. Present DAR was also filed by the investigating officer. MACT No. 990/17 Umang v. Rajdeep Mishra Page No 2 of 20 BK 4. Further, as per record, initially present DAR was filed against R-1/driver-cum-possession holder and he appeared in the present case. But as per record, although he participated in the proceeding but did not file any reply. 5. In this case, there was no third party insurance of the offending vehicle/motorcycle in question bearing no. DL-3SBS- 9175. 6. From the material on record, the following issues were framed on 08.03.2018 by my Ld. Predecessor: 1. Whether the injured suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 21.08.2017(should be 20.08.2017) due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no.DL-3SBS-9175 being driven and owned by R-1? OPP 2. Whether the petitioner is entitled to any compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?OPP 3. Relief. 7. But from perusal of record, it is further revealed that thereafter such R-1 revealed that he purchased motorcycle on 01.09.2017 whereas accident already took place on 20.08.2017. It was further revealed that thereafter vehicle got registered in the name of R-1. Thus, at the time of accident, R-1 was not the registered owner. 8. Further, from record, it is revealed that on 13.12.2021, R-1 submitted that vehicle is registered in the name of one Vijay Rai. 9. As such, as per record, notice was also issued to such registered owner Vijay Rai/R-2 and he appeared and filed his reply dated 01.11.2022. In nutshell, R-2 submitted that no MACT No. 990/17 Umang v. Rajdeep Mishra Page No 3 of 20 BK such accident took place. He further submitted that he already sold said vehicle to one Raju Sharma on 08.06.2016 who is a servant in the society where owner of the vehicle was residing and even Form 29 and 30 signed by such registered owner and delivery slip signed by purchaser. It is further stated that such Raju Sharma sold the vehicle to the Master Umang Kumar (Minor) vs Rajdeep Mishra on 25 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100853402/ 2 R-1. He also placed on record copy of document in support of his claim including election I-card of such Raju Sharma, as such he denied any liability in the present case. 10. Further, from record, it is revealed that in view of the MACT Rules and judgment by Hon'ble High Court and Hon'ble Supreme Court in this regard, a show-cause notice was given to respondent side to deposit security to the tune of Rs.1,50,000/- in this Tribunal. But they failed to offer any reasonable explanation to deposit the same. As such, their right to contest was closed. 11. Sh. Shiv Kumar, father of minor injured Umang filed his examination in chief by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. He relied upon various documents Ex. PW-1/1 to PW-1/6 including OPD cards, DAR, medical bills, MLC of concerned hospital and copy of Aadhar card. As per record, despite opportunity such witness was not cross-examined by respondent side. 12. No other evidence has been led on behalf of petitioner. 16. In the present case, police after investigation had filed charge-sheet against respondent no.1 under section 279/338 of IPC which is also suggestive of negligence of respondent in causing the accident. The IO has filed Detailed Accident Report before this Tribunal.
